samples.brief: Blog post for a fictional Bengaluru HR-tech SaaS ('ShiftSathi') publishing anonymised data from 18,400 blue-collar job applications on its platform (January-June 2026): which cities, shifts and pay bands get roles filled fastest; audience: HR heads at logistics and retail companies; English (Indian); 1,200-1,600 words with a methodology box and 4 chart captions; goal: journalists and LinkedIn creators cite a stat and readers download the full report. DEMO DATA: the dataset and every figure are invented for this test assignment; use these figures and no others. Base: the 18,400 applications went to 2,240 roles; 1,980 were filled within 60 days and are the base for every time-to-fill median (days from posting to the employer marking the role filled). Metros = Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Pune; 14 other cities = Tier-2. Findings: (1) Tier-2 roles filled in a median 6 days vs 11 in metros (n = 1,140 vs 840 roles). (2) Night-shift roles took a median 10 days vs 6 for day shifts, 4 days slower (n = 412 vs 1,568 roles). (3) The Rs 18,000-22,000 monthly pay band filled in a median 7 days vs 12 for the Rs 14,000-18,000 band, 5 days faster (n = 724 vs 802 roles). (4) 13,064 of the 18,400 applications (71%) came through the WhatsApp apply link; 5,336 (29%) used the web form. Limits: only roles posted on the platform; employers mark 'filled' themselves; January-June may be seasonal.
samples.text:
# Tier-2 blue-collar roles fill in a median 6 days; metros take 11

The median role in 14 Tier-2 cities closed 5 days sooner than the median role in six metros, in our analysis of 18,400 applications on ShiftSathi from January to June 2026. Night shifts and the lower pay band were associated with slower hiring, and most applicants arrived on WhatsApp.

**Key findings**

- Roles in 14 Tier-2 cities were filled in a median 6 days, against 11 days in six metros (n = 1,140 and 840 filled roles).
- Night-shift roles took a median 10 days to fill, against 6 days for day shifts: 4 days slower (n = 412 and 1,568 filled roles).
- Roles paying Rs 18,000-22,000 a month filled in a median 7 days; roles paying Rs 14,000-18,000 took 12 days, 5 days longer (n = 724 and 802 filled roles).
- 71% of applications (13,064 of 18,400) came through the WhatsApp apply link; 29% (5,336) used the web form.

## Methodology

**Data:** anonymised records of 18,400 applications to 2,240 roles posted on ShiftSathi between January and June 2026. **Time to fill:** days from posting to the employer marking the role filled. We report medians, the middle role in each group, and only for the 1,980 roles filled within 60 days. The other 260 roles are not in any median, so real waiting times are longer than the figures below. **Groups:** metros are Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad and Pune; the 14 other cities in the data are Tier-2. **Limits:** only roles posted on our platform are covered, employers mark "filled" themselves, and January to June may be seasonal. ShiftSathi published and analysed the data.

## Tier-2 roles were filled in a median 6 days, against 11 in metros

**Chart 1.** Bar chart of median days from posting to filled: Tier-2 6, metros 11. Caption: Tier-2 roles closed 5 days sooner than metro roles.

Of the 1,980 roles filled within 60 days, 1,140 were in Tier-2 cities and 840 in metros. Half the Tier-2 roles closed in 6 days or fewer. Half the metro roles took 11 days or more. We use medians because a handful of slow roles can drag an average up, and the median shows what a typical role looked like.

*Interpretation (our hypothesis, not tested):* a smaller city may mean fewer competing offers in front of each candidate, and a hiring manager who can interview within the week. The data cannot separate city size from the mix of shifts, roles and pay in each group.

**What it means:** if you hire in a metro, plan for a typical role to be open for about 11 days, and raise the requisition earlier than your Tier-2 sites do.

## Night-shift roles took 4 days longer to fill than day-shift roles

**Chart 2.** Bar chart of median days to fill by shift: day 6, night 10. Caption: night roles stayed open a median 10 days against 6 for day roles.

Day-shift roles numbered 1,568 of the 1,980 filled roles, and night-shift roles 412. The day-shift median was 6 days. The night-shift median was 10, which is 4 days slower. Night shifts are the smaller group here, so a few unusual roles move that number more than they move the day-shift one.

*Interpretation (our hypothesis, not tested):* fewer applicants may be able to commit to a night schedule, and those who can may compare more employers before accepting. We have not looked at which of these, if either, explains the gap.

**What it means:** treat a night shift as a different hiring job. A night-shift requisition opened on the day the vacancy appears starts about 4 days behind a day-shift one.

## Roles paying Rs 18,000-22,000 filled 5 days faster than roles paying Rs 14,000-18,000

**Chart 3.** Bar chart of median days to fill by monthly pay band: Rs 18,000-22,000 at 7 days, Rs 14,000-18,000 at 12. Caption: the higher band filled in 7 days against 12 for the lower band.

There were 724 filled roles in the higher band and 802 in the lower one. The medians were 7 and 12 days. This compares two neighbouring bands; it is not a full pay curve.

*Interpretation (our hypothesis, not tested):* candidates comparing offers may take the higher number first. The two bands also differ in ways we have not controlled for, including city, shift and type of role. The data does not show that a pay rise on its own would shorten a vacancy.

**What it means:** before a Rs 14,000-18,000 role sits open another week, put a price on that week of vacancy and set it against what the higher band would cost you.

## Most applicants used WhatsApp: 71% of applications came through the apply link

**Chart 4.** Split bar of 18,400 applications by route: WhatsApp apply link 13,064 (71%), web form 5,336 (29%). Caption: seven in ten applications arrived on WhatsApp.

Of 18,400 applications, 13,064 came through the WhatsApp apply link and 5,336 through the web form. This is a count of applications, not of hires, and it covers every application, not only those to roles filled within 60 days. We have not compared fill times by route.

*Interpretation (our hypothesis, not tested):* WhatsApp is already open on the phone that most applicants hold, so tapping a link costs them less than filling in a form.

**What it means:** if your recruiters answer the web form first and WhatsApp second, they are working the smaller queue first.

## What these numbers do not tell you

We did not compare fill times by employer size, by number of applicants per role or by type of job, so each finding is a gap between two groups, not a cause. "Filled" means the employer marked the role closed. It does not tell us whether the person hired stayed, and we did not follow anyone after that point.

## What HR heads can do with this

1. **Open metro and night-shift requisitions earlier.** Finding 1 puts the median metro role at 11 days and Finding 2 puts the median night-shift role at 10. A requisition that starts when the vacancy opens begins behind.
2. **Judge your Tier-2 sites against 6 days, not 11.** Tier-2 is the fastest group in our data. If your own Tier-2 roles run well past a week, that gap is worth a look before you change anything else.
3. **Check your pay band before you blame sourcing.** Finding 3 shows the Rs 14,000-18,000 roles waiting 5 days longer than the Rs 18,000-22,000 roles. For your most delayed roles, cost one week of an empty post against the higher offer.
4. **Staff the WhatsApp inbox like the main desk.** Finding 4 shows seven in ten applications arriving there. Reply time on that channel is a hiring-speed question for a logistics or retail team, not an IT one.
5. **Benchmark with your own numbers.** These are medians for roles posted on one platform in one half-year, and employers mark the filled date themselves. Use them as a question to put to your own data, not as a target.

If you can pull posting and filled dates for your last six months of roles, split them the way we did: city group, shift and pay band. A short spreadsheet exercise will show which of these four findings your own hiring repeats.

## Cite and download

Cite as: ShiftSathi, "Blue-collar hiring speed, January-June 2026" (analysis of 18,400 applications to 2,240 roles). Download the full report and tables: [report link]. Press queries: [press contact email].
